prompt: A small lamp warms the corner beside a folded cloth.
Rain rattles the glass while the roof answers in low knocks.
A brass key lies under the bowl although nobody put it there.
A friend brings one pear and waits beside the table.
The blanket rests on the chair near a quiet yellow light.
Two wet footprints stop in the middle of the dry floor.
The other child shares a pencil and watches Leo draw.
Thunder rolls beyond the garden and the door shakes once.
Cold wind bends the branches and pushes water under the gate.
A closed music box begins one note and then becomes silent.
Grandmother sits nearby and cuts warm bread into two pieces.
Morning light reaches the cup on the still kitchen table.
A red marble rolls uphill when every hand is far away.
A shy visitor leaves a drawing and stays long enough to listen.
White rain jumps from the stones while dark clouds hide the trees.
A cup of milk cools beside the soft blue curtain.
Three chalk circles appear outside without a single track.
Someone returns Leo's lost button and smiles without speaking.
The reading chair waits beneath a gentle green shade.
A bright flash arrives before the loud sky breaks open.
The neighbour gives Leo half an apple and keeps the other half.
Heavy drops race along the gutter as the chimney groans.
Warm socks dry beside the stove on the wooden floor.
One feather falls inside although every window is closed.
A cousin remembers Leo's cup and pours a little water for him.
The quiet kettle stands near a clean towel and a warm plate.
Wet branches tap the wall and the cellar door knocks below.
A silver bell rings twice but its string never moves.
Fast rain fills the yard while a low cloud covers the fence.
The pillow keeps a small hollow where a head was resting.
A blue thread enters a crack in the wall and does not return.
The younger child offers a biscuit and sits close by.
A clean towel hangs near the basin in the peaceful room.
Four pebbles form a square after everyone has gone inside.
Wind pulls at the shutters while water drums above the ceiling.
An old friend carries two oranges in and gives Leo the brighter one.
The quiet girl brings a paper boat and asks where it should sail.
The fence leans under a hard gust and every loose pane answers.
A tiny light crosses the empty hall and disappears at the stairs.
The reading lamp makes a calm circle over the open book.
A wooden block is warm on one side though the room is cold.
Hail skips across the roof and gathers beside the dark window.
A boy waits at the step until Leo makes room beside him.
Soft bread rests under a cloth near the evening cup.
A long rumble crosses the field and the porch light trembles.
The clock loses a minute and finds it again before noon.
The curtain holds a pale square of sun across the rug.
Auntie listens to Leo's small story before telling her own.
Rain sweeps sideways beneath the porch and rattles the latch.
The new child lends Leo a red crayon without being asked.
The wooden floor is cool but the little coat beside it is warm.
A paper star turns toward the door when no air is moving.
Five drops remain on the glass after all the others slide away.
Evening light settles on the bowl and the folded napkin.
A visitor saves the last chair for Leo and waits for him.
The trees bow together as thunder travels behind the hill.
A neighbour knocks softly and brings back the borrowed spoon.
After supper the small room smells of soap and warm tea.
A white stone appears in the shoe that was empty a moment ago.
A sudden gust scatters leaves while rain flashes under the gate.
The little scarf waits beside the door where the air is gentle.
Two children move closer so Leo can see the picture between them.
Water runs down the chimney and the roof speaks in quick beats.
The final candle makes two shadows although only Leo is near.
What does a quiet light keep when everyone is asleep?
What changes inside when the sky becomes loud and close?
Where can an unanswered question wait without disappearing?
How can you tell that another person chose to stay?
